records.name: NASA FIRMS — VIIRS active fire detections (NRT)

WORLDVIEW must never ship a shared key. GEV merges NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Suomi-NPP 24 h windows with a 30 min cache. The FIRMS map viewer's Esri basemap is NOT covered by NASA's policy (NASA forum thread p=21423) — irrelevant to the CSV API but do not screenshot the FIRMS viewer for docs.

records.name: readsb (local receiver) — user's own ADS-B/Mode-S decoder output
records.termsUrl: n/a — data originates from the user's own receiver
records.license: No third-party data policy (user-generated). readsb software is GPL-3.0 and is NOT distributed by WORLDVIEW (software.json readsb)
records.notes: Default only when the user configures a receiver; otherwise inert. Reception of 1090 MHz broadcasts is lawful in most jurisdictions but not all — the user, not WORLDVIEW, is the operator. If the user's readsb also feeds aggregators, that is between the user and the aggregator. WORLDVIEW must not upload receiver data anywhere.

records.name: AISStream.io — live AIS via websocket
records.license: No formal licence or ToS published (GEV DATA_SOURCES.md line 24: "Free, beta, no formal ToS; AIS is a public broadcast"). Documentation (read 2026-09-21) states "no SLA or uptime guarantee", 3 connections/account, "Direct browser connections are not permitted"
records.notes: User supplies their own API key (Electron main holds it; renderer never sees it — satisfies "Direct browser connections are not permitted"). No published licence means commercial use is unknown, not prohibited; the 24 h normalized-retention cap and export=false are WORLDVIEW's conservative defaults, not provider terms, and can be relaxed after a human reads whatever terms AISStream publishes or answers by email. AIS messages themselves are public safety broadcasts; the encumbrance, if any, is on the aggregated feed.
